ForwardVarianceCurve.description:
Forward variance curve ξ₀(t) for rough volatility models.

Represents `ξ₀(t) = E^Q[V_t | F₀]`, expected instantaneous variance under
the consuming model's pricing measure. Values are supplied or calibrated by
the caller. The integral sets the model's expected accumulated variance.

Differencing ATM implied total variance is an optional proxy, not an exact
variance-swap bootstrap. This type interpolates the supplied curve; it does
not perform market calibration.

interpolation.description: Interpolation contract used by the constructor.

times.description: Point times or interval ends (strictly increasing year fractions).

values.description: Point samples or constant interval variances (all > 0).

HurstExponent.description:
Validated Hurst exponent H ∈ (0, 1).

The Hurst exponent determines the roughness of fractional Brownian motion:

- H < 0.5 — rough (anti-persistent increments)
- H = 0.5 — standard Brownian motion
- H > 0.5 — smooth (persistent increments)

description: Cheyette + rough stochastic volatility model parameters.

hurst.description: Hurst exponent H ∈ (0, 0.5) for the rough vol driver.

kappa.description: Mean reversion of the short rate (κ > 0).

phi_times.description: Time knots for the initial forward rate curve φ(t) = f(0, t).

phi_values.description: Value knots for the initial forward rate curve φ(t) = f(0, t).

rho.description: Correlation between rate and vol innovations ρ ∈ [-1, 1].

sigma_base.description: Base volatility term structure σ₀(t) for the rate process.
